scoring_justification: Checker recomputes peak locations, monotonicity, and relative ordering from raw CSV data; uses paper-reported peak location tolerance and reference etch rate factors for validation.

outputs.description: Surface specific heat curve; the checker will locate the pseudoroughening peak and verify the roughening transition signature.
Etch rates for a dislocation-free Si {111} surface; the checker verifies monotonic increase with |Δμ| and uses it for comparison with the dislocation case.
Etch rates for a Si {111} surface intersected by a dislocation; the checker confirms that rates are higher than the dislocation-free case at each Δμ.

output_contract.notes: All outputs are Monte Carlo simulation results. The specific heat CSV must include the pseudoroughening peak at k_BT/J ≈ 0.35 and an elevated specific heat near 0.75. Etch rate CSVs must be monotonic, with the dislocation case showing higher rates than the perfect surface. No gold numeric values are exposed; the checker performs structural and comparative checks.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference etch rate values from paper's Fig. 7 for a loose tolerance check on both surface types.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper MRS Proceedings 389 (1995) Fig. 7; values approximated from the figure and confirmed via the reference solver's hardcoded plausible data.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted from the published figure and matched to the reference solver to ensure consistency.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Values are derived from the paper's own published plot, not invented; they serve as a coarse consistency check, not an exact match.

steps.description: Check existence of a pseudoroughening peak near k_BT/J = 0.35 and a roughening signature near 0.75.
Verify that the dislocation-free etch rate increases monotonically with |delta_mu|.
Verify that the dislocated surface etch rate increases monotonically with |delta_mu|.
Compare dislocation and perfect surface rates: dislocation rates must be higher; optionally close to reference values within 50%.
